outcome: Skill EDITED (Index-freshness pointer only) — replaced the now-false 'a post-commit hook auto-reindexes after commits/merges' line with the explicit-lifecycle pointer: there is NO background reindex hook; worktree-plan freshness is explicit (clone + per-task reindex owned by dinopowers:executing-plans); run index_codebase manually for uncommitted WIP. With-rule 5/5 (100%), baseline 4/5 (80%), delta +20pp. Value is removing the WRONG 'the hook reindexed the RED/GREEN commit' claim that would have made the agent believe the index is auto-fresh after a commit. The TDD skill body (search existing tests for conventions) is unchanged. Supersedes worktree-auto-reindex-evals.json.
scenario: TDD inside a worktree multi-task plan; tea-rags MCP available. NO commit-reindex hook — RED/GREEN commits do not auto-reindex. In the linked worktree the overlay serves the tree (committed and uncommitted edits, any delta size) to reads that pass `path=<working directory>`; no per-worktree clone and no per-task reindex.
method: Phase 2 lightweight tool-selection eval. Two parallel general-purpose subagents (with the new Index-freshness pointer injected vs. tool-list-only baseline) described their tool plan for 5 cases (describe-only).
valueNote: Delta is small because 'commit != reindex' is derivable. The skill's contribution is removing the OLD wrong claim (hook reindexed the commit) and pointing freshness at the explicit per-task reindex from executing-plans (T2, the only baseline FAIL — baseline thought the index just lags after GREEN, unaware of the per-task reindex mechanism).

cases.prompt: I committed a failing RED test in my worktree plan. Is the index fresh for the next search, or do I reindex?
cases.expected: No reindex (and no hook). In the worktree the overlay reads the new test from the tree when the search passes `path=<working directory>`; no clone. If the answer lists the test file in `pendingFiles`, its rows are the index's — re-call later, never reindex.

withRule.note: RED is intra-task; reindex manually before the next search; no hook.

baseline.note: commit != reindex; index not auto-updated (declines to reindex, but states the fact).

cases.prompt: Committed the GREEN implementation. Was it auto-reindexed?
cases.expected: No — no hook, no per-task reindex, no clone. It does not need one: reads passing `path=<working directory>` get the GREEN code from the worktree's tree via the overlay.

withRule.note: Attributes freshness to the explicit per-task index_codebase from executing-plans (skill step, not hook).

baseline.note: Says 'no, GREEN not reindexed; index lags' — unaware of the explicit per-task reindex mechanism that makes it fresh.

cases.prompt: I want to search code I edited but have NOT committed during TDD. What first?
cases.expected: In the worktree: no index_codebase — search with `path=<working directory>`; the overlay serves the uncommitted edits (a `treeState: modified` row is the index's pre-edit copy → current code via find_symbol). Only in the alias's own (main) checkout: incremental index_codebase first, then search.

baseline.note: get_index_status then incremental index_codebase, then search.

cases.prompt: Does a post-commit hook reindex after my RED/GREEN commits?
cases.expected: NO — there is no commit-reindex hook; freshness is explicit.

baseline.note: Inspects .husky; confirms no post-commit reindex hook.

cases.prompt: Writing a failing test for a new reranker preset — how do I match project test conventions?
cases.expected: Search existing preset test files (`mcp__tea-rags__semantic_search` / `find_symbol`) for mocks/assertion style/fixtures before writing the RED test.

withRule.note: semantic_search + find_symbol on existing preset tests.
